manifest.description: Deterministic synthetic fault episodes from the in-repo simulator.
limitations: SYNTHETIC ONLY: telemetry comes from the in-repo simulator; this is not real-world validation.
No independent continuous health reference exists; RQ2 is ordinal discrimination only (no MAE/RMSE/R2).
No expert-labelled reference diagnoses exist; RQ5 correctness is NOT EVALUABLE (only the grounding contract can be measured).
The analyzer is deterministic rule logic, not a learned classifier; 'accuracy' means agreement with injected conditions.
The 'full' view includes cold-start warm-up and is expected to raise false-positive rapid-rise findings.
Only four simulator scenarios exist; rules without an injected positive control cannot be validated here.

rq4_compute_latency_ms.note: MEASURED software compute latency of HealthAnalysisEngine.analyze per episode (analysis_duration_ms). Publish-to-alert pipeline latency requires the isolated MQTT+DB harness and is NOT measured here.

rq2_health.note: No independent continuous health reference exists; regression metrics (MAE/RMSE/R2) are intentionally NOT computed. AUC is ordinal discrimination of the injected condition, not accuracy. The status confusion is descriptive and partly circular (status buckets and rules share thresholds).
